cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.30)

add_library(urge-binding STATIC)

# The `*.cc` below were regenerated by `bind/gen_binding.cmake`, which the
# top-level CMakeLists.txt includes before this directory.  Two consequences:
#
#   * the glob sees whatever that run wrote, so a brand new binding_*.cc is
#     compiled without a second configure;
#   * a class that did not exist when the tree was last configured is only in
#     the *fresh* glob, so the first configure after adding a header needs the
#     whole glob re-expanded, which is what CONFIGURE_DEPENDS covers.  It is
#     set on this directory only: it is the one that depends on generated files.
file(GLOB BINDING_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/*.cc")
target_sources(urge-binding PRIVATE ${BINDING_SOURCES})

# `ruby-static` is normally the interpreter third_party/cruby compiles from
# source.  When bind/external supplies a prebuilt one there is nothing to
# compile, so the same name is defined here instead, as an INTERFACE library
# that carries only what a consumer needs: the include path, the import
# library, and the marker the host reads to tell the two interpreters apart.
#
# `ruby-msvc` comes first on the include path on purpose.  The drop-in ships a
# config.h generated by a MinGW build (`include/ruby-<ver>/x64-mingw64/`), which
# MSVC cannot read; the arch directory holds nothing else, so replacing it with
# our own `ruby/config.h` costs nothing and is the whole reason that directory
# exists.  See the comment at the top of it.
#
# The import library needs the same treatment, for a different reason: the one
# dlltool produced defines the C runtime functions the interpreter calls
# (`round`, `fclose`, `getenv`, ...) as well as Ruby's own API, which MSVC
# cannot link beside its own CRT.  `filter_import_lib.py` rewrites it into an
# archive that describes the interpreter and nothing else -- again, see the
# comment at the top of the file for why dropping those members beats
# `/FORCE:MULTIPLE`.  The rewrite runs here, in the configure step, the same way
# the binding glue is generated, and writes into the build tree so that
# bind/external itself is only ever read.
if(URGE_EXTERNAL_RUBY_DIR)
  find_program(URGE_PYTHON NAMES python python3 py)
  if(NOT URGE_PYTHON)
    message(FATAL_ERROR
      "bind/external needs a Python interpreter to rewrite the CRuby import "
      "library; none was found on PATH.")
  endif()

  set(URGE_RUBY_LINK_LIB "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/ruby-import.lib")
  execute_process(
    COMMAND "${URGE_PYTHON}"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ruby-msvc/filter_import_lib.py"
            "${URGE_RUBY_IMPORT_LIB}" "${URGE_RUBY_LINK_LIB}"
    RESULT_VARIABLE URGE_FILTER_RESULT
    OUTPUT_VARIABLE URGE_FILTER_OUTPUT
    ERROR_VARIABLE URGE_FILTER_OUTPUT)
  if(NOT URGE_FILTER_RESULT EQUAL 0)
    message(FATAL_ERROR
      "filter_import_lib.py failed on ${URGE_RUBY_IMPORT_LIB}:\n"
      "${URGE_FILTER_OUTPUT}")
  endif()

  add_library(ruby-static INTERFACE)
  target_include_directories(ruby-static INTERFACE
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ruby-msvc"
    "${URGE_RUBY_INCLUDE_DIR}")
  target_link_libraries(ruby-static INTERFACE "${URGE_RUBY_LINK_LIB}")
  target_compile_definitions(ruby-static INTERFACE URGE_EXTERNAL_RUBY=1)
endif()

target_include_directories(urge-binding PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})
target_link_libraries(urge-binding PUBLIC ruby-static urge-core zlibstatic)

# libffi backs the Win32API binding (binding_win32api.cc), which uses it to call
# a DLL export whose signature is only known at runtime.  The dependency is
# Windows-only for the same reason the binding is: `third_party/CMakeLists.txt`
# only brings the library up there, and off Windows the binding compiles to an
# empty initialiser that needs nothing from it.
if(WIN32)
  target_link_libraries(urge-binding PUBLIC libffi)
endif()
